items.title: AI Proved the Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis. What Happens Now?
items.excerpt: Unlike other recent AI proofs, this one has been unpacked by human experts. The implications, one mathematician said, are “staggering.”

history_match.title: AI's failed attempt to crack the Riemann hypothesis led a mathematician to a breakthrough

items.title: AI researchers stranded Claude on a virtual desert island. It started to “play.”
items.excerpt: In various tests, solo AI agents invented versions of basketball and “the floor is lava.” But were they truly playing?

items.title: “We were looking at it wrong”: The explosive claim that’s upended the AI world
items.excerpt: An exclusive interview with Nick Cammarata, the researcher whose 26,000-word viral blog post has AI safety folks celebrating.

items.title: AI chatbots could help mental health but also reinforce harmful thinking
items.excerpt: Curtin University's Warren Mansell proposes a framework arguing chatbot conversations can either broaden a person's perspective or trap them in repetitive reassurance-seeking, depending on emotional state, goals and how the chatbot responds. The framework has yet to be tested empirically.

items.title: When LLMs are trained on frivolous online content, they can get brain rot like humans do
items.excerpt: Texas A&M researchers trained four LLMs on low-quality, attention-grabbing Twitter posts and saw weaker reasoning and memory, more skipped reasoning steps and looser ethical responses. Retraining on higher-quality data did not fully restore performance.

items.title: Smartphone chatting and payment habits help AI identify daily stress, small study finds
items.excerpt: KAIST researchers built SHIRBT-MMF, which groups repeated smartphone behaviors like messenger chatting and payments by purpose to estimate daily stress. In a 26-person study, personalized models flagged stress days with about 75% accuracy, beating app-usage baselines.

items.title: Researchers improve weather forecasts looking two to six weeks out
items.excerpt: A new technique significantly improves weather forecasting beyond two weeks. Researchers developed a machine-learning model that learns to correct errors in existing forecasting models to make their output more accurate over the two-to-six-week time frame, a key window for emergency planning.

history_match.title: AI-enhanced weather model doubles predictive power two to six weeks out

items.title: Claude just found a CRISPR-like DNA pattern, but even Anthropic's scientists aren't sure what it does
items.excerpt: The large language model took less than a day to identify the curious stretch of DNA

items.title: Grounding AI agents in biological reality: Building blocks for autonomous wet labs
items.excerpt: Google Research describes building blocks for grounding AI agents in real wet-lab biology, a step toward autonomous laboratories that plan and run experiments.

history_match.title: Hybrid Digital Twins Developed for Future Autonomous Labs

items.title: Putting Earth AI to work: Geospatial agents for our planet's biggest challenges
items.excerpt: Google Research introduces geospatial agents built on its Earth AI foundation models, letting researchers query planetary data to tackle problems such as disasters, climate and public health.

history_match.title: Unlocking Earth AI's planetary geospatial foundation models for global public health

items.title: World's fastest AI-powered racing drone outflies the best human pilots
items.excerpt: An AI-operated drone learned to fly from scratch and navigated a race course at speeds over 60 mph, using a single camera.

items.title: Physicists develop early warning system that predicts when an AI is about to go rogue
items.excerpt: A new mathematical formula tracks an AI's internal "compass needle" to flag undesirable outputs before they happen.

history_match.title: Simple math formula predicts when AI chatbots will go rogue

items.title: AI can act exactly like a human, but we still don't think it's conscious
items.excerpt: A new study reveals that people draw a surprisingly sharp line between human consciousness and artificial intelligence, even when both behave identically. Researchers found that participants considered even the most responsive AI less conscious than the least responsive human. Yet when asked about "awareness" instead, people judged humans and AI much more similarly.

history_match.title: Even when AI behaves just like us, people still rate it as less conscious than humans

items.title: AI reveals a hidden chemical shortcut that could turn CO2 into fuel
items.excerpt: Scientists used artificial intelligence to uncover nearly 10,000 chemical reactions involved in transforming carbon dioxide into fuels and chemicals, revealing crucial pathways that traditional models had missed. The discovery dramatically improved predictions of CO2 conversion and uncovered a surprising hydrogen reaction that could inspire more efficient catalysts.

history_match.title: Using machine learning and computation to unveil mechanisms for CO2-to-fuel conversion

items.title: Danaher, Nvidia Combine Lab Instrumentation and AI to Advance Autonomous Science
items.excerpt: The partnership is part of broader efforts at Danaher to provide AI-powered solutions that help scientists make discoveries faster.

items.title: Can math stay human in the age of AI?
items.excerpt: As AI churns out mathematical proofs, a DeepMind study raises a bigger question: What do we lose when we focus only on the answers?

items.title: '24/7 unmanned synthesis platform' uses robots and light to produce drug candidates
items.excerpt: KAIST chemists paired robotic reagent dispensing with visible-light continuous-flow reactors and inline analytics to convert furans into N-methyl pyrroles, a common drug scaffold. The unattended platform worked on more than 20 compounds and scaled up production.

items.title: AI reads centuries-old handwriting to reveal Britain's vast historic shipping trade
items.excerpt: University of Southampton researchers used AI to transcribe about 100,000 pages of handwritten port records, building a database of hundreds of thousands of British voyages from the late 1500s to the mid-1700s.
